title: Calculate server capacity
summary: A function is a reusable piece of code that turns inputs into an output. In JavaScript, return sends the result back. We will use one to estimate how many servers a service needs.
example: Math.ceil(2.5) returns 3. Rounding up matters because you cannot run half a server.
takeaway: Divide incoming requests per second by the capacity of one server, then round up. Both inputs use the same unit.
instruction: Complete serversNeeded(requestsPerSecond, capacityPerServer). Return the smallest whole number of servers that can handle the traffic. Requests are non-negative and capacity is always positive.
hint: Use Math.ceil(requestsPerSecond / capacityPerServer). Zero traffic needs zero servers in this simplified model.

title: Route the next request
summary: Round-robin routing takes turns across servers. An array is an ordered list; JavaScript indexes start at 0. The remainder operator (%) wraps a request number back to the start of that list.
example: For three servers, request indexes 0, 1, 2, 3 use server indexes 0, 1, 2, 0. For example, 3 % 3 is 0.
takeaway: Use servers[index] to read an array item. Return null if the array is empty, because no server is available.
instruction: Complete pickServer(servers, requestIndex). Return the server for this zero-based request index using round-robin routing, or null when servers is empty. The index is a non-negative integer.
hint: Check servers.length first. Otherwise return servers[requestIndex % servers.length].

tests.label: First request goes to server a
Fourth request wraps around to a

title: Read through a cache
summary: A cache lookup checks for a saved value before doing slower work. JavaScript objects hold key-value pairs. Object.hasOwn(object, key) tells you whether a key exists, even when its value is 0 or an empty string.
example: The cached value 0 is still a hit. Testing if (cache[key]) would incorrectly treat it as missing.
takeaway: Check whether a key exists, not whether its value is truthy. Use the database as the fallback on a miss.
instruction: Complete readValue(cache, database, key). Return the cached value if the cache owns the key. Otherwise return the database value, or null if neither object owns it. Values are strings or numbers.
hint: Check Object.hasOwn(cache, key), then Object.hasOwn(database, key), then return null.

tests.label: Cache hit wins over the database copy
Zero is a valid cached value
Empty string is a valid cached value
